content.user_title: Guide Stella Through Her Final Choice
content.value_statement: Final chapters need a clear emotional structure and meaningful player choices. This guide provides scenes, dialogue, and endings for a science-fiction roleplay finale.
actual_capabilities: Sets up rescue and self-repair scenarios for the final chapter.
Guides a character through reflection on earlier survival and research events.
Presents balanced reasons to return to Earth or remain on Gaia.
Supplies three core ending paths and an epilogue framework.
Provides emotional dialogue cues for a player-character conversation.
limitations: It is a story guide, not a playable game engine.
It assumes the Stella Chen and Gaia setting from earlier chapters.
It does not track player choices or generate persistent game state.
The dialogue is primarily written in Chinese with embedded English phrases.

use_cases.title: Finish a roleplay campaign
use_cases.description: Use the scenes to close a long-running survival roleplay with a meaningful final decision.

use_cases.title: Draft a branching finale
use_cases.description: Adapt the ending structure when writing a science-fiction story with several valid conclusions.

use_cases.title: Practice emotional scene design
use_cases.description: Study the reflection, conflict, and closure beats in the chapter before drafting original scenes.

prompt_templates.title: Start the finale
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Planning the Escape to begin the rescue scenario. Present Stella with the incoming Earth signal and ask what she feels.

prompt_templates.title: Explore the decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Roleplay Stella as she weighs returning to Earth against staying on Gaia. Ask me for advice without choosing for me.

prompt_templates.title: Create a tailored ending
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the guide to create an ending where Stella returns to Earth as an ambassador. Include callbacks to survival, research, and the Eos friendship.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt Planning the Escape for my original alien-planet story. Keep three meaningful endings and replace all setting-specific details.

output: An Earth rescue signal arrives with a 72-hour extraction window.
Stella looks at her camp and asks whether returning home is still what she wants.
Stella explains that Gaia has become her home and that the Eos need a bridge between worlds.
She sends a respectful message declining rescue and begins planning a permanent research station.
Stella repairs the ship and returns to Earth with a plan for peaceful official contact.
The ending frames her as an ambassador who will return to Gaia.

best_practices: Ask the player about earlier choices before selecting an ending path.
Treat each ending as valid and avoid presenting one as morally correct.
Adapt the dialogue pace to the player response and emotional comfort.
anti_patterns: Do not force Stella to choose an ending before the player can discuss the conflict.
Do not remove callbacks to earlier events when using the finale in a campaign.
Do not treat the supplied setting details as factual information outside the story.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps you run or write the final chapter of a branching science-fiction roleplay.

faq.question: Does it choose an ending automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides options and dialogue so the player can influence the decision.

faq.question: Can I use it for an original setting?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace the names, locations, and prior events with details from your story.

faq.question: Is this a game engine?
faq.answer: No. It is a narrative guide and does not manage state, rules, or saved choices.

faq.question: Which endings are included?
faq.answer: The guide covers returning to Earth, staying on Gaia, and becoming a bridge between both worlds.

faq.question: What language is the source dialogue in?
faq.answer: The source dialogue is mainly Chinese and includes some English phrases.
